item.title: China’s Laser Leap: Beijing Is Quietly Winning the Next Arms Race
item.description: China seems to have outpaced the United States and its allies in the development of directed energy weapons—as seen by its recent exports to the Middle East. The post China’s Laser Leap: Beijing Is Quietly Winning the Next Arms Race appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Japan’s Nuclear Talk Just Woke a Sleeping Dragon—and a Madman
item.description: Japan’s recent militaristic rhetoric has provoked the wrath of North Korea—but no one in Asia has any idea how Pyongyang will actually respond yet. The post Japan’s Nuclear Talk Just Woke a Sleeping Dragon—and a Madman appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: America Is Paying the Price for Backing Jihadists in Syria
item.description: During “Operation Hawkeye Strike,” the United States bombed jihadist targets across Syria—but what use were the strikes when their targets’ ideological brethren now run the government? item.title: Why the UK Is Getting a New Artillery Gun

item.title: Why Do Fighter Jet Canopies Look So Weird?
item.description: As time has gone on, innovations in fighter jet technology have made “bubble cockpits” steadily more useful to pilots—and more expensive to maintain. The post Why Do Fighter Jet Canopies Look So Weird? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Does America Have an “Air National Guard”?
item.description: Though one might imagine the “Air National Guard” as a secondary force using refurbished equipment to defend America’s borders, it regularly deploys to conflict zones with modern fighter jets. item.title: How Russia’s MiG-29 Fighter Jet Fell from Grace
item.description: Russia’s MiG-29 fighter was more than capable of matching America’s F-16 Fighting Falcon and similar aircraft—but the Kremlin failed to keep it relevant over time. The post How Russia’s MiG-29 Fighter Jet Fell from Grace appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Six Minutes in Caracas: How US Special Forces Grabbed Nicolas Maduro
item.description: The raid on Venezuelan dictator Nicolas Maduro’s compound in Caracas—involving units from the US Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marines—highlighted the US military’s extreme proficiency at inter-service operations. item.title: Nicolas Maduro Is Gone. Now What?
item.description: Despite the capture of Venezuelan dictator Nicolas Maduro, the remainder of his regime is still in power in Caracas—raising difficult questions for how the Trump administration should proceed. The post Nicolas Maduro Is Gone. Now What? appeared first on The National Interest.
